text:
tess: quick flag 1: after we rolled codegen-quant4 to beta routes overnight i'm seeing an uptick in identifier-hallucination on the code-complete slice (users report wrong function names). overall accuracy looks flat but hallucination rate +1.2pp on that slice.

omar: painful. did the safety gates catch this?

build-bot: deploy codegen-quant4 -> beta routes completed at 1835007000. no autofallback events.

nina: pasted sampled failures:
```
Input: "Implement parse_user in auth_service"
v1: "def parse_user(token):\n    # uses jwt..."
v2(quant4): "def parse_user_auth(token):\n    # uses jwt..."  <-- renamed, breaks infra binding
```

tess: that renaming breaks downstream bindings (integration tests expect parse_user). this is a correctness hallucination, not graceful rename. we need a guard for API-stable identifiers.

omar: what are current rollout rules?

tess: rules: fallback if any slice hallucination_rate_delta >= 1.5pp OR global quality delta <-2% over 1h. but hallucination metric wasn't enabled for code-complete slice until yesterday. onboarding gap.

nina: slice traffic: code-complete ~3.5k req/day, peak 200 req/hr. recent dump shows hallucination_count 42 -> 84 in 12h window, rate 1.2% -> 2.4%.

omar: so absolute delta +1.2pp but below the 1.5pp cutoff. we need a specialized rule for identifier hallucinations because small absolute changes cause customer breakage. propose: per-route hard cutoff: if identifier_hallucination_rate >= 1.5% AND samples >= 500 in window => immediate rollback. also add a paired-coverage check: if renamed identifier appears in >10% of samples and is not present in ground-truth mappings => flag.

tess: yes. also implement a heuristic to detect renamed defs: regex match for def/func names and map to expected symbol table. if mismatch rate > 0.7% escalate.

ops-bot: note: rollout policy can accept new metric keys. add `identifier_hallucination_rate` as a first-class metric.

nina: test plan: run `rb eval --model codegen-quant4 --slices code-complete --metrics identifier_hallucination_rate,exact-match --window 2h` and run 1k contrastive pairs where v1 is ground truth code.

omar: also deploy a quick integration test in staging that pulls latest samples and runs symbol-resolution smokechecks against our repo-mock. failing tests should trip canary.

tess: decision: pause further ramp to beta; open hotfix PR to add identifier_hallucination metric to rollout config and new per-route hard cutoff: `if identifier_hallucination_rate_delta >= 1.0pp AND samples >= 500 => immediate fallback` (temporary until we tune).

omar: make it a two-window rule: delta persists over 2 consecutive 15m windows to avoid transient noise.

nina: PR opened: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/rollouts/pulls/431 (draft) 1 — includes unit tests and a migration to add metric column to rollout_events.

ops-bot: rollout-policy update queued; apply-on-merge: true.

omar: also add Datadog monitor `redwood.metrics.identifier_hallucination` for affected routes; set alert threshold at 1.0% with 15m aggregation and notify eng-oncall as warning.

tess: follow-up: add a small synthetic harness that validates function names against repo fixtures during onboarding so quantized variants can't silently rename core APIs. i'll sketch the harness and drop it in tests/identifier_harness.

nina: running the contrastive judge now (n=1k). will paste summary when done.

omar: good. main takeaway 1: metric onboarding gaps bite. treat identifier hallucination as high-sensitivity for code routes and add per-route absolute cutoffs + consecutive-window confirmation.

tess: agreed. tagging legal/devtools to inform customers if rollback happens. thanks all.
